title: Token velocity sentinel: microbenchmark harness and regression pipeline
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Build and maintain a stable, CI-driven microbenchmark suite ("Token Velocity Sentinel") to track tokens/sec and p95 generation latency for core models and model families. The harness should produce deterministic, repeatable measurements across releases, detect regressions automatically, and integrate with our CI and runbooks. Key goals: (1) produce per-model baseline distributions for tokens/sec and p95 under controlled workloads, (2) surface regressions with a low false-positive rate using statistical control techniques, (3) provide artifacts (dashboards, golden traces, PR comments) to accelerate root cause and rollback, and (4) be lightweight enough to run in pre-merge CI canaries and nightly stability runs.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline includes a Token Velocity Sentinel job that completes within 20 minutes for core models
Per-model baseline metrics (tokens/sec mean/std, p95) are stored in our metrics backend with tags: model, quantization, seq_len, batch_size
Automatic regression detector evaluates new runs against baseline and opens an alert when threshold breached (configurable sensitivity)
Run artifacts (event traces, raw token timelines, and a summary report) are posted to the PR and linked in the CI job
Dashboard exists with historical trends and per-model control charts for tokens/sec and p95
tasks: Design synthetic workload templates (short/medium/long seq lengths) and representative prompt corpus
Implement runner harness with jittered request inter-arrival and configurable concurrency profiles
Instrument harness to capture per-request token throughput, generation latency (per-step), and batch packing stats
Integrate baseline store and comparator; implement EWMA + control-chart based detector with hysteresis
Wire CI jobs: lightweight pre-merge smoke, nightly full sweep, and canary run for Dedicated deploys
Create dashboard panels and alerting rules; document runbook for false-positive triage
comments: 2025-11-03 Priya K: Kickoff — drafted initial design doc and benchmarking matrix. Decided to target 3 representative seq lengths: 32, 256, 1024. Using synthetic tokenizers to keep runs deterministic.

2025-11-04 Liam O: Implemented prototype harness that replays request traces and captures per-step times. Found a large variance in tokens/sec for small batch sizes on older kernels. Added option to pin kernel version in runner.

2025-11-05 Priya K: Review feedback from runtime team — suggested adding KV-cache warmup traces to better reflect streaming workloads. Also flagged need for per-model thresholds instead of global thresholds.

2025-11-06 Engineering review: Chose EWMA with two-sigma control limits and 24-hour decaying baseline to balance sensitivity and noise. Decided to store summaries in metrics backend and raw traces in S3 for 90 days.

2025-11-07 Liam O: PoC PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 — includes harness, baseline serializer, and CI job definitions. Requesting review from @runtime-team and @observability. CI smoke job currently runs on a small GPU fleet; nightly job needs capacity slot reservation.
notes: Unique focus: combine deterministic synthetic traces with KV-cache warmup and EWMA-based regression detection to minimize false positives while catching meaningful throughput regressions. Aim to cover both hosted and dedicated runtime variants.
next_steps: Address PR feedback from runtime team about kernel pinning and batching env vars
Add model-specific threshold tuning for MPT-7B, Llama2-13B, and internal finetuned models
Schedule nightly capacity for full-sweep runs and add canary hook for dedicated rollout testing
